candidates.explanation: The snippet is truncated, so I could not see this code. The 422 means the stored user has provider = 'google'. Registration goes through AuthService.register and UsersService.create, and neither shows any code that sets the provider to google. So the likely cause is the usersRepository.create({...}) call at the end of create. It probably sets provider to google, or to some other non-email value. candidates.explanation: The snippet is truncated, so I could not see this code. The 422 means the stored user has provider = 'google'. Registration goes through AuthService.register and UsersService.create, and neither shows any code that sets the provider to google. So the likely cause is the usersRepository.create({...}) call at the end of create. It probably sets provider to google, or to some other non-email value. The original code uses createUserDto.provider ?? AuthProvidersEnum.email.

register calls usersService.create with ...dto and sets role and status. It does not set provider explicitly. If the provider default in create is wrong, or the DTO can supply a provider, the user is stored with the wrong provider. This is a less likely cause.
This is where the error is raised, when user.provider !== AuthProvidersEnum.email. The check itself looks correct, so this is a symptom and not the root cause.

fix.description: In UsersService.create, set provider: createUserDto.provider ?? AuthProvidersEnum.email in the object passed to usersRepository.create. Do not default it to google. I could not see that line, so check it against the full file.
